searchText: is there are writeup why TTD is used to perform this upgrade instead of block number? I remember seeing explanation about it somewhere but I cannot find it now https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3675#terminal-total-difficulty-vs-block-number (the anchor linked to specifically) One of our engineers (<@757155006175641691>) wrote a script to track the difference and as you can see from this graph of Ropsten over the last couple hours its not an easy relationship to explain: Will mev-boost be ready for the merge or is it just a 'nice-to-have'? Is it also expected to be disabled during the actual merge process? Anyone have any tips for watching Goerli play out? What will be the first sign that Goerli was a success? Could be a twitter account to follow, or actual metrics to watch imo mev-boost would in no way delay the merge and the intention is to have something ready for the merge, mev-boost is live on several testnets and being incorporated to merge testing efforts yep this is the rough consensus, following the PR here: https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/pull/38 I see. You'll wait some CONSTANT # of epochs before pinging the external builder network? the constant we settled on was 0 essentially want to finalize past the transition then as soon as that has happened, honest validators are free to use the remote builder network The word honest is doing some work here 😆 Sounds good though. honest: "following the spec as written" byzantine agents can arbitrarily deviate and it is on the protocol design to be tolerant to that
